message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 130, "amount_cents": 8178}, {"order_id": 133, "amount_cents": 6783}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work. I'll start by checking the refund ledger against the handoff claims.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, with the same two orders and amounts. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm those refunds apply to real orders before trusting the ledger.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and both refunds fall on real orders with amounts below the order totals. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer in the batch, starting with acme, rather than doing the arithmetic myself.
Acme's net balance of 28879 matches my own check (orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, minus refunds 8178 + 6783 = 14961, gives 28879). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 70733 matches the order total (37666 + 33067 = 70733) with no refunds, so it checks out. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance.
Cobalt's net of 16841 matches its orders (10547 + 6294) with no refunds, so all three balances check out against the ledger. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 70733 matches its order total with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 16841 matches its order total with no refunds, and I already verified it, so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.

All three customers have been paid their verified net balances: acme 28879, birch 70733, cobalt 16841. Each balance matched the order totals less the refunds Alpha reported, and every record_payout call returned ok.
